Subject: Private GPU runways — egress-aware topology & sustained-throughput validation

Jordan / Acme ops,

Thanks again for the call this morning. I wanted to capture the follow-up items and propose a short validation plan so we can finalize the committed throughput in the SOW. High-level asks:

- Confirm the 24-hr sustained target: 5k tokens/sec aggregate (all tenants). Your on-call said peak windows are ~10–15 minutes at ~2x baseline.
- Share any egress limits per VPC (we saw notes about a 2 Gbps per-AZ cap). If that’s enforced, it affects batching headroom and quantization choices.
- We'll run a 2-hour stress validation from our staging cluster against your preprod VPC. We need a service account and a small routing ACL for the test window.

I've attached a runway_calc_v3.xlsx with our warm-pool sizing assumptions (page 2) and a sample egress capture to illustrate expected packet sizes. Proposed dates: Jan 12–13 (US PST windows) for the validation run.

Next steps for us once you confirm the egress cap and grant the service account: finalize the warm-pool sizing and a short mutual action plan.

Thanks —
Sergio

- Egress: nominal 2 Gbps per AZ, but we can open to 3 Gbps on the upcoming maintenance window (Jan 12 02:00–06:00 UTC) if needed. Need a justification for sustained bump.
- Service account: created as redwood-staging@acme-svc. I’ve sent an IAM invite to sergio@redwood.com.

We also have a soft constraint on connection counts from our edge LB — ~5k concurrent TCP flows without sticky sessions.

Jordan

Team —

Thanks Jordan for the fast response and for provisioning the service account. A few internal notes before we kick the run:

1) Egress sensitivity: if Acme keeps to 2 Gbps, our runway_calc shows we must reduce batch width by ~30% to stay under the cap which raises token cost by ~12% and increases p95 latency in the 100–200ms range for long-context requests.

2) Connection cap: 5k TCP flows without stickiness means we should exercise our multiplexing config (single-connection reuse per client) during the run. Karthik, please prepare a multiplexing recipe and set of client run profiles.

3) Warm-pool sizing: I’d like the test to validate a 5-minute warm-up target for a single AZ failure scenario. Mina, add a checklist for KV-cache warmup and model shard priming.

If Acme can open the 3 Gbps window during Jan 12 maintenance, we can run the full-shot stress test; otherwise we'll run a constrained validation (reduced batch widths) and capture telemetry for a follow-up run.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Platform Ops, Redwood Inference

Jordan / team —

I've sketched the multiplexing + batching recipe we'll use for the run and attached a short runbook (in the drive link). Key bullets:

- Client profile A: baseline steady-state (500 concurrent streams, keep-alive, reuse TCP connection per client).
- Client profile B: microburst (7200 tokens/sec for 10 mins, 2 minutes ramp down).
- Batching strategy: adaptive max-batch 128 for short-context, max-batch 32 for 4k+ contexts to keep p95 under 350ms.
- When egress < 2.5 Gbps, auto-reduce batch width by 25% and enable quantization-level-2.

I'll instrument detailed counters (batch sizes, egress bytes/sec, concurrent connections, KV cache hit %) and push dashboards ahead of the run. Marissa, can you own the post-run ops notes and handoff to CS?

-Karthik
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
